test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 1 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In which of the following years did the Government of India initiate the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (NP-NSPE)
solution:
The correct answer is __**1995**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The government of India initiated the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (NP-NSPE) on **15 August 1995**.
 
• The objective of the scheme is to help improve the effectiveness of **primary education** by improving the nutritional status of primary school children.
 
• Initially, the scheme was implemented in **2,408 blocks** of the country to provide food to students in classes one through five of government, government-aided and local body run schools. By 1997–98, the scheme had been implemented across the country.
 
• Under this programme, a cooked midday meal with **300 calories **and **12 grams** of protein is provided to all children enrolled in classes one to five.
 
• In **October 2007**, the scheme included students in upper primary classes of six to eight in 3,479 educationally backward blocks, and the name was changed from National Programme for Nutrition Support to Primary Education to National Programme of Mid Day Meals in Schools.
 
• Though cooked food was to be provided, most states (apart from those already providing cooked food) chose to provide "**dry rations**" to students.
 
• "**Dry rations**" refers to the provision of uncooked 3 kg of wheat or rice to children with 80% attendance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Food & Nutrition Board (FNB), set up in **1964**, is an attached office of the Ministry of Women & Child Development and has a countrywide set up.
 
• Originally with Ministry of Food, the FNB was shifted to Ministry of Women and Child Development (then Department of WCD) in **1993**.
 
• The current minister for the Ministry of Women and Child Development is **Smriti Irani**.
 
• The **Midday Meal Scheme** is a school meal programme in India designed to better the nutritional standing of school-age children nationwide.
